Sur les 18 122 textes en vigueur détenus, 1 503 ne le sont pas, faute d’en détenir le libellé d’aujourd’hui (seul l’original modifié depuis, une version plus récente que l’éditeur ne publie pas en fichier, ou un texte publié seulement en allemand) : Lex les nomme et n’y répond pas comme au droit d’aujourd’hui.
served.sentence_en: Lex holds 24,302 Luxembourg texts, 16,619 of them served as today's law. Of the 18,122 texts in force held, 1,503 are not, because today's wording is not held (only the original amended since, a newer version the publisher does not publish as a file, or a text published only in German): Lex names them and does not answer from them as today's law.

shape.label_fr: Codes (états du code, XML de l’éditeur)
shape.reason: Each code is ONE long document with its own outline (livre, titre, chapitre, article) and a chain of dated states; the act row is typed (address, type, dates, status: every code carries them, from the publisher). A question reaches it by the code's name (alias, by code) or its routing line, then the outline walk inside it (7quater). Splitting a code into a pile of articles would lose the outline, its cheapest signal (5B:63).
